newsitem.title: USA: U.S. HMO stocks rally on United Healthcare report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. HMO stocks rally on United Healthcare report.

text.p: Most U.S. health maintenance organization stocks rallied Thursday on growing optimism about 1997 that was bolstered by comments from United Healthcare Corp, and amidst a broadly bullish market.
Shares in United Healthcare -- the nation's largest HMO company -- were up 2-1/8 to 50-3/4.

The company Thursday reported lower fourth-quarter profits versus the year-ago period on an operating basis, but also said it sees no signs of medical cost inflation breaking above its present rate of four to five percent.
The Minneapolis-based giant also said it was able to raise premiums an average of five percent in its key January commercial plan renewal period.
"United's indication of five percent price increases was the main factor" behind Thursday's rally, said Volpe Welty healthcare industry analyst Ed Keaney.
Oxford Health Plans Inc shares were up 2-7/8 to 58-7/8; Aetna Inc was up 3-3/4 to 86; PacifiCare Health Systems Inc was up 2-1/16 to 83-3/8.
Over the past week or two, HMO profits have come in at generally lower levels, as expected, but the outlook for this year is improving, analysts said.

"The earnings and the conference calls are confirmation of a better 1997 for the whole HMO group and that's set against the background of a hot market today," said Dain Bosworth healthcare industry analyst Chris Sergeant.
